context:
AuroraLedger is a fictional supplier-risk service testing a new address comparison feature. Identity means the contracting legal organization; location and parent group remain separate concepts. The pipeline has candidate generation, feature extraction, scoring, edge policy, resolution and master selection stages. Today's “experiment” compares yesterday's production run to a developer run on a fresh source extract. Both candidate generation and threshold settings changed, and an intermediate feature cache may contain data from a newer normalization library. The developer reports a higher pair F1 but did not retain all entity outputs.

There are 2,000 reviewed pairs collected over six months, with repeated organizations and source-pair imbalance. Review timestamps and adjudicator disagreements are available. The team can run two isolated replays on a fixed snapshot, but it has not specified a temporal or entity-disjoint split, code/data manifests, access policy or downstream acceptance thresholds. Changing production is outside scope. False merges can contaminate risk alerts; missed links can hide exposure. Runtime matters, but the complete-output cost has not been reconciled.

Design the smallest reproducible experiment that can attribute a change to the proposed feature. Compare an unchanged baseline and one controlled alternative, pin stage contracts and reuse only demonstrably compatible artifacts. Explain leakage, candidate recall, pair and entity outcomes, uncertainty and critical slices. Distinguish repeatability, behavioral agreement and real identity evidence. Specify success/falsification/inconclusive rules and next actions without inventing completed results or mandating a workflow platform.
title: AuroraLedger reproducible scorer comparison
